title: Dedicated: tiered autoscaling, burst controls, and fleet utilization reporting
author: Priya Singh
description:
Motivation: Customers running Dedicated capacity need predictable throughput guarantees while still supporting short-duration traffic spikes. Current autoscaler treats all Dedicated pools the same which can lead to overprovisioning or degraded tail latency during bursts. This PR introduces tiered autoscaling policies, per-pool burst credits, and a new utilization reporting pipeline to inform SLOs and billing.

Summary of changes: 1) Autoscaler: add policy types (steady, burst-aware, conservative) and policy selector based on pool labels and commit-config. 2) Burst controls: per-pool burst window and credit accounting (max_burst_tokens, refill_rate). Backend enforces short-term burst ceilings with graceful degradation (reject -> queue -> fallback routing) once credits are exhausted. 3) Utilization reporting: new metrics export (redwood.dedicated.pool_utilization, burst_credit_used) aggregated per-hour and per-pool; includes delta-based ingestion to reduce metrics cardinality. 4) API: exposed new pool-config fields in the admin API and Console with validation and defaults. 5) Tests + docs: unit and e2e tests for policy selection, credit accounting; docs and console screenshots.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked (ENG-1287)
- [x] Unit tests for autoscaler and credit accounting
- [x] Integration tests for fallback routing and metrics emission
- [x] Console panel for utilization and burst status
- [x] Backwards compatible: default policy is 'steady' to match current behavior

Commits (high-level):
- feat(autoscaler): add tiered policy types and selector (4 commits)
- feat(burst): implement burst token accounting and enforcement hooks (6 commits)
- feat(metrics): emit pool_utilization and burst_credit_used metrics (3 commits)
- api(admin): add pool config schema and validation (2 commits)
- ui(console): add utilization widget and edit form (3 commits)
- test: add unit+integration tests, e2e harness changes (5 commits)

Changed areas (high level):
- services/autoscaler/* (policy engine, tests)
- services/burst-controller/* (token bucket impl, enforcement)
- services/metrics/exporter/* (aggregation and export)
- api/admin/v1/pool_config.go (schema, validation)
- web/console/src/components/dedicated/UtilizationPanel.tsx (ui)
- infra/helm/charts/dedicated/values.yaml (defaults for refill_rate/max_burst_tokens)

Testing & rollout:
- CI: full unit and integration suite ran, flake fixed by retry in e2e; blue/green rollout plan for Dedicated to allow fast rollback.
- Staged rollout: default policy on existing pools remains 'steady'. New pools created after deploy default to conservative until customers opt in. Canary rollout to 10% of clusters for 48 hours with elevated logging.

Notes on backwards compatibility: Pool config additions are optional; system picks default values for older configs. Metric names are additive and do not break existing dashboards.

Related: Linked Linear tickets ENG-1287 (policy design), ENG-1342 (billing metrics), and follow-up ENG-1403 (auto-tuning suggestions), internal incident SUP-912 referenced as example traffic pattern that motivated burst credits.

CI Summary: initial CI run had one flaky e2e failure (timing) which was addressed by improving test harness timing assumptions; final CI run: all checks passed.

Merge: squashed and merged to main after approvals.
conversation:
Reviewer: Jordan Lee: Could you clarify how we compute refill_rate units?
Author (Priya Singh): Refill_rate is tokens per second scaled by pool_parallelism; we document default math in the admin API doc.
Reviewer: Alex Navarro: What happens to queued requests when credits deplete during a burst?
Author: We attempt shallow queueing (up to 200ms) then route to configured fallback model or return overload response depending on pool policy. Added integration test for this behavior.
Reviewer: Maya Chen: Add observability for rejected/overflowed requests so SRE can tune policies.
Author: Added metrics redwood.dedicated.pool_rejections and redwood.dedicated.pool_overflows; dashboard screenshot included.
Reviewer: Jordan Lee: Please ensure upgrade path for existing helm charts.
Author: Updated infra/helm/charts/dedicated/values.yaml with defaults and migration notes.
Approvals: Jordan Lee approved, Alex Navarro approved after requested docs tweaks.
release_notes: Added tiered autoscaling policies for Dedicated pools, per-pool burst credit controls, and new utilization metrics for improved SLOs and billing accuracy.
